newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were little changed Friday ahead of a cooler weekend throughout most of the Northeast and Midwest, industry sources said.
"The market was pretty quiet this morning. There were a lot of people missing so prices held," one Midwest trader said.
Louisiana Gulf prices at the Henry Hub were talked an average of two cents higher at $2.18-2.22 per mmBtu, with Transco (Station 65) quoted mostly in the low-$2.20s.
Conversely, south Texas prices eased by two cents to about $2.10 as cooler forecasts dampened cooling demand in the state.
In the Northeast, New York city-gate prices were well supported by cooler weather forecasts through early next week, as most deals were reported done in the mid-$2.40s.
Appalachian prices, however, were steady to lower at $2.35-2.36 on Columbia and the low-$2.40s on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices fell two cents to about $2, with Demarcation quoted mostly at $2.01.
Chicago city-gate values were quoted at $2.23-2.27.
In west Texas, Permian prices lost six cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s, while prices at the southern California border slipped an equal amount to about $2.03-2.04.
Temperatures in the Southwest are expected to remain warmer-than-normal through early next week.
